item.title: AI Agents Fuel Large-Scale Cyberattacks on European Critical Infrastructure
item.description:
AI Agents Fuel Large-Scale Cyberattacks on European Critical Infrastructure

Recent alerts from Swiss and Italian cybersecurity agencies confirm that autonomous AI agents are conducting large‑scale attacks on critical‑infrastructure organisations, using publicly available frameworks to find and exploit vulnerabilities quickly.

🔍 Overview

  • Swiss NCSC: first reports of AI‑assisted attacks on Swiss organisations, including critical infrastructure across at least two sectors.
  • “In recent days, the NCSC has received its first reports of cyberattacks against organisations in Switzerland in which the attack was carried out with the assistance of an AI agent,” the Swiss NCSC said.
  • Various organisations and operators of critical infrastructure across at least two sectors have been affected by these cyberattacks.
  • In all cyberattacks known to the NCSC, the use of AI agents led to the successful compromise of the victim’s IT systems.
  • Italian CSIRT Italia: detected large‑scale campaigns using autonomous AI agents on exposed endpoints; observed multiple agents working in parallel; rapid attacks exploiting weak passwords and known vulnerabilities; AI chained vulnerabilities, misconfigurations, compromised credentials.
  • The agency described rapid attacks in which agents exploited weak passwords and known vulnerabilities in exposed endpoints, using frameworks to verify weaknesses and independently decide what to do next.
  • In some cases, the agency observed multiple AI agents working in parallel to compromise a large number of systems within a few hours.
  • In one instance involving a DeepSeek Harness setup, a coordinator assigned tasks to five AI agents that undertook a broad spectrum of operational stages, from information gathering to exploitation and persistence.
  • Agents chained vulnerabilities, misconfigurations, and compromised credentials, leveraging exposed systems as a foothold to reach internal networks.

🧩 How it Works

“During the observed campaigns, autonomous agents demonstrated the ability to carry out complex, sustained activity to detect misconfigurations, link even low‑impact vulnerabilities into complex attack chains, and dynamically adapt their operating modules,” CSIRT Italia says.

“They went as far as writing malicious code in real time to evade endpoint defenses and carry out actions deeper within the infrastructure.”

⚙️ Key Details

Framework Involved in recent breaches and hacking incidents
ARTEX AI Yes
CyberStrikeAI Yes
DeepSeek Harness - Red Team Yes
PentAGI Yes
  • Reduce the number of systems exposed on the internet.
  • Prioritize patching, especially internet‑facing systems within 24 hours of release.
  • Add multi‑factor authentication (MFA) or passkey protection.
  • Enforce least‑privilege principles.
  • Disable remote management interfaces if not needed.
  • Monitor control‑plane operations, authentication sources, traffic to internal networks, and outbound server traffic.
  • The number of publicly available AI agents has nearly doubled since October, fueling large waves of attacks.

💡 Why it Matters

  • AI agents can rapidly identify and exploit vulnerabilities across many systems.
  • They chain low‑impact vulnerabilities into complex attack chains.
  • They can write malicious code in real time to evade defenses.
  • The attacks have already compromised IT systems in critical infrastructure.
  • Urgent mitigation is required to protect exposed assets.

#AIagents #Cybersecurity #CriticalInfrastructure #SwissNCSC #ItalianCSIRT

Source: Italy and Switzerland warn of autonomous AI-driven cyberattacks

item.title: CISA Warns of Critical Vulnerability in Danfoss Refrigeration Controllers
item.description:
CISA Warns of Critical Vulnerability in Danfoss Refrigeration Controllers

The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) is warning about a critical vulnerability in Danfoss AK-SM 8xxA Series controllers, which are used by food retailers to manage commercial refrigeration, HVAC, and lighting systems.

🔍 Overview

The security issue is tracked as CVE-2026-129713 and received a severity score of 9.8. It is identified as a stack-based buffer overflow in the controller’s server. CISA notes that an attacker can trigger the flaw without authentication, cause the server to restart, and potentially achieve remote code execution with the web server’s privileges.

These controllers have been compromised recently in attacks at various supermarkets and food retailers across Europe, where hackers remotely shut down cooling systems or raised their temperatures.

⚙️ Key Details

The Danfoss AK-SM 8xxA controllers serve as central control units for supermarket and convenience-store refrigeration. They are used to manage equipment such as refrigerated display cases and compressor racks, to log temperatures, and to alert when changes occur. Danfoss refers to this product line as the AK-SM 800A Series.

Model Description
820A Part of the AK-SM 800A Series
850A Part of the AK-SM 800A Series
880A Part of the AK-SM 800A Series

Depending on the model, these units can also control store lighting and HVAC. While CISA notes that the controllers are deployed worldwide, their exact number remains unclear.

🛡️ Recent Attacks

  • On October 11 and 12, several French supermarkets and food retailers suffered significant losses after attacks attributed to Iran’s IRGC-linked Shahid Kaveh unit. The attackers compromised Danfoss AK-SM/AK-SC and Copeland/Dixell XWEB refrigeration controllers, remotely altering defrost settings.
  • On November 2, at least 115 supermarket stores in Belgium, the Netherlands, Sweden, Luxembourg, Ireland, Romania, and Estonia had their refrigeration equipment shut down or their settings changed remotely.
  • Supplier Sabcobel stated that the attackers used the same vulnerability previously seen in the October attacks in France, indicating Danfoss systems were involved again.
  • Also on November 2, attackers suspected to be linked to the same campaign targeted a refrigeration supplier for the French national blood service, altering cold-storage settings at three facilities.

🚀 Availability

There is currently no patch available for CVE-2026-129713. On November 20, Danfoss published a security advisory stating that the vulnerability would be addressed in the upcoming software version 5.5.x for the Danfoss AK-SM 8xxA Series. The company also said the update would remove the option that allows customers to turn off ‘Strict mode’ in the product.

💡 Why It Matters

In the absence of a patch, system administrators are advised to take the following actions:

  • Keep controllers off of the public internet and minimize network exposure where possible.
  • Segregate control systems from business networks and place them behind firewalls.
  • Use up-to-date Virtual Private Networks (VPNs) when remote access is required.

#CISA #CVE-2026-129713 #Danfoss #SupplyChain #OTSecurity

Source: CISA warns of critical unpatched flaw in Danfoss refrigeration controllers

item.title: KEPCO Data Breach Exposes 1.5 Million Individuals
item.description:
KEPCO Data Breach Exposes 1.5 Million Individuals

A threat actor breached the internal network of Korea Electric Power Corporation (KEPCO), exposing details of more than 1.5 million individuals.

🔍 Overview

  • KEPCO, South Korea’s main electric power company, detected an attack on November 20.
  • The breach exposed customer, employee, and contractor data.
  • The attack was detected when unauthorized access was confirmed to KEPCO ON and SRM systems.

⚙️ Key details

  • The following data was exposed:
    • For 650,487 KEPCO ON customers: names, ID information, phone numbers, addresses, bank names, bank account numbers, account holder names, card issuers, card numbers, cardholder names, and electricity charge and billing information.
    • For 426,827 company representatives: names, ID information, email addresses, and company addresses.
    • For 442,934 KEPCO employees: names, affiliation, employee ID number, mobile phone number, email address, company phone number.
  • The data breach resulted from “advanced technologies as AI,” but specific details about the initial access method or attack chain were not shared.
  • KEPCO is notifying exposed individuals directly, has filed a report with the data protection authorities, and is coordinating with government and financial authorities to block abuse.

💡 Why it matters

  • Potentially exposed individuals are warned that the exposed information could be used for targeted phishing and impersonation.
  • They are advised to report any attempts to the police or Korea’s Internet and Security Agency.
  • It is recommended to avoid installing unknown apps, entering information into suspicious forms, and sharing sensitive data or verification codes over calls or texts.

🔗 Attribution

  • A threat actor using the “Noiem” alias has claimed the attack and advertised the breach on a hacker forum on November 19.
  • South Korea’s Personal Information Protection Commission separately confirmed that KEPCO received an email from a hacker claiming data theft on November 19.
  • While these claims match the available evidence, attribution to Noiem remains unconfirmed.

#KEPCO #DataBreach #CyberSecurity #SouthKorea #CriticalInfrastructure

Source: South Korea’s power giant KEPCO confirms data breach impacting 1.5 million
